items.title: The Government of Canada, together with the Province of Ontario, invests in strengthening trade capacity and supply chain resilience through the Port of Sault Ste. Marie
items.teaser: Today, the Honourable Steven MacKinnon, Minister of Transport and Leader of the Government in the House of Commons, announced an investment of up to $125 million through the Trade Diversification Corridors Fund to support the development of the Port of Sault Ste. Marie, led by the Hamilton-Oshawa Port Authority. This investment will fund a series of improvements to unlock the Port's potential as a key transportation and trade hub, increasing its cargo-handling capacity to more than 3.5 million metric tonnes annually by 2031, a three-fold increase over current volumes. The project is expected to create 2,150 direct and 2,600 indirect jobs while strengthening supply chains and supporting economic growth across Northern Ontario and beyond.

items.title: Biographical Notes – Mariève B. Tremblay
items.teaser: Ms. Mariève B. Tremblay is a senior executive, lawyer and corporate director with more than 25 years of leadership experience across the transportation and logistics, energy, mining, and industrial sectors. items.title: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework
items.teaser: The Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada jointly review and renew the Bank’s monetary policy framework every five years. The Bank then independently conducts monetary policy to achieve the framework’s goals. The Government and the Bank agree that monetary policy must work to promote the economic and financial well being of Canadians. We also agree that the best way monetary policy can do this is by keeping inflation low, stable, and predictable, thereby protecting Canadians from large increases in the cost of living. A credible and well understood monetary policy framework that focuses on price stability helps the economy grow, supports investment and job creation, and fosters confidence in Canada’s economy.

items.title: Building a stronger Canada through a well-managed, predictable immigration system

Last year and through Budget 2025, we committed to taking back control over the immigration system and putting Canada on a trajectory to bring immigration back to sustainable levels.
